pages.text: Photosynthesis converts light energy into glucose. This process happens inside the chloroplasts of plant cells, using water and carbon dioxide.
The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast. They produce ATP and NADPH, which the Calvin cycle later uses to build sugars.
Cellular respiration happens in the mitochondria. It consumes oxygen and glucose to produce ATP, releasing carbon dioxide and water.
